profile.headline: Embedded Software Engineer
profile.summary:
Software engineer with extensive experience developing embedded software and low-level system software:
- Experience developing high-integrity bare-metal firmware in C and Ada for ARM-based and
   RISC-V-based microcontrollers and SOCs.
- Experience developing operating systems kernel-level software for  HP-UX, AIX and Windows.
- Experience porting kernel-level software from Solaris to HP-UX and from Linux to AIX.
- Experience developing low-level networking/multi-threaded software.
- Experience using industry best practices for developing high-quality software such as Fagan 
  inspections, pair-programming, design-by-contract and test-driven development.
- Experience producing technical deliverables for the entire software development lifecycle, 
  including requirements specifications, design specifications and test plans.
- Experience leading small teams of developers (3-4 developers).
- Experience teaching Software Engineering and Programming courses.

Professional beliefs: 
- I believe that Today's complex software, especially high-integrity embedded software,  should be designed to  
   be self-checking to catch defects in itself automatically, during initial development, testing, maintenance and 
   production. 
- I believe in using formal methods to design and verify high-integrity software
- I believe in using safer programming languages that can catch more defects at both compile-time and
    runtime, especially Ada (and even more so SPARK Ada) for high-integrity embedded software.
- I believe in the rigorous use of programming-by-contract principles to write self-checking code in any 
    programming language.

positions.title: Embedded Software Engineer
positions.description:
Bare-metal firmware development
- Designed several key aspects of the high-integrity firmware architecture for the safety monitor
processor of the latest self-driving on-board computer of Tesla vehicles, including an innovative memory protection architecture for ARM Cortex-M and Cortex-R MPUs and for the
RISC-V PMP.
- Designed and implemented the whole Ethernet stack for the safety monitor subsystem,
including writing a bare-metal Ethernet MAC and PHY drivers and integrating a zero-copy port
of the FreeRTOS TCP/IP.
- Wrote bare-metal drivers for various CPU-architecture-dependent peripherals such as memory protection units (MPUs), interrupt controllers, timers for both ARM and RISCV.
- Architected and implemented a highly-portable mailbox-based RPC framework for inter-core communication between the safety monitor processor and the application processors of the onboard self-driving computer.

positions.title: Embedded Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Bare-metal firmware development
- Linux kernel driver development

positions.title: Embedded Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Designed and implemented a Linux kernel bus driver and ancillary drivers
  for the management complex (MC) hardware module of QorIQ LS2 SoCs.
- Designed and implemented a driver for u-boot, for loading and booting the
  MC firmware.
- Designed and implemented a user-space tool to do dynamic resource management
  of Layerscape MC objects, such as creation/destruction of MC objects and
  their assignment to child MC containers.
- Designed and implemented a UEFI network driver (SNP driver) for the NXP
  QorIQ DPAA2 Ethernet interface.
- Designed and implemented the memory protection unit (MPU) support for the
  embedded software of a point-of-sale device, running on a Kinetis microcontroller
  and FreeRTOS.

positions.title: Software Development Engineer
positions.description:
System software development for Windows Hyper-V:
- Designed and implemented several enhancements in the Windows 
  kernel components of the virtual PCI (VPCI) bus subsystem, as 
  part of the feature that provides SR-IOV support for 
  network virtualization in Hyper-V, for Windows 8. 
- Designed and implemented a prototype for doing live migration of Hyper-V
  virtual machines over RDMA in user-mode using the Network Direct API.  
- Designed and implemented a Hyper-V kernel-mode component for doing
  live migration of a virtual machine's RAM over SMB/RDMA.

positions.title: Software Engineer IV
positions.description: Developed a utility to remotely manage blade servers in a Cisco UCS cluster (via UCSM XML APIs) and Linux/KVM hypervisors running on them (via libvirt APIs). Functionality included facilities to query hardware resources in the UCS cluster, power on/off blade servers, create/destroy/start/stop/pause virtual machines, P2V, live migration of virtual machines across blade servers and allocation of dynamic VNICs to virtual machines to leverage pass-through switching capabilities of Cisco Palo VN-link network adapters.

positions.title: Advisory Software Engineer
positions.description:
AIX system software development:
- Lead engineer for the porting of the OFED RDSv3 protocol for 
  InfiniBand from the Linux kernel to the AIX kernel. This work 
  required detailed knowledge of the OFED network stack as 
  implemented on Linux as well as of the Linux kernel APIs for 
  device drivers in order to design corresponding wrapper APIs for
  the AIX kernel.
- Designed and implemented the IP over InfiniBand connected mode 
  support for the TCP/IP stack of AIX.
  This work required detailed knowledge of the network interface 
  layer of the AIX kernel TCP/IP stack and the AIX kernel InfiniBand 
  stack APIs.
- Designed and implemented the trace buffer manager kernel 
  component of the ProbeVue product, a dynamic tracing tool for 
  AIX. Also, I lead the initial integration of the whole product.
- Implemented various enhancements and bug fixes for the AIX 
  kernel Runtime Error Checking framework, a self-checking feature 
  of AIX to catch bugs both in testing and production.
- Developed coding guidelines and training material for runtime 
  detection of defects close to their root cause, for AIX kernel 
  developers. Delivered training to all departments in the AIX 
  development organization. Also, developed coding guidelines for 
  defect prevention, for AIX kernel and user-space developers.

positions.title: Graduate teaching assistant
positions.description:
Teaching assistant for the Models of Software Systems course
in the Master of Software Engineering program.

positions.title: Adjunct Lecturer
positions.description:
Mentor of students in the West-coast Master of Software Engineering 
program, in the area of Formal Methods.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
System software development for Storage Appliances:
- Designed and implemented performance enhancements for the
  online consistency checker of the WAFL file system.
- Designed and implemented a memory sampling mechanism
  for the ONTAP kernel (an embedded operating system for storage 
  appliances), to take periodic snapshots of key kernel data 
  structures, for debugging purposes.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
HP-UX system software development:
- Ported the ONC+2.3 NFS distributed filesystem client
  from the Solaris kernel to the HP-UX kernel. This work required
  detailed knowledge of both HP-UX and Solaris core kernel 
  subsystems such as virtual filesystem (VFS), virtual memory (VM) 
  and process management (PM).
- Developed components of a performance measurement tool that 
  used dynamic binary code instrumentation/translation techniques.

positions.title: Systems Integration Consultant
positions.description:
- Developed custom software components as part of implementing a
  generic billing package for several Internet companies.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Networking application software development for multiple platforms, including  MSDOS, Win32, UNIX, and Unisys mainframes:
- Developed a gateway between the Telnet and Poll/Select 
  protocols, to provide  remote login from Windows NT workstations
  to UNISYS V series mainframes.
- Developed a file transfer system that integrated UNISYS A series 
  mainframes,  UNIX servers and PCs.
- Developed a terminal emulator for MS-DOS and Windows NT/95 
  PCs that included slave printing and file transfer facilities, and 
  supported several types of terminals and communication protocols.
- Developed a gateway between the BNA-I and BNA-II networks to 
  communicate Unisys mainframes.

projects.title: HiRTOS
projects.description: A multi-core RTOS written in SPARK Ada. This project won the 2023 Ada/SPARK embedded crate of the year (https://blog.adacore.com/ada-spark-crate-of-the-year-2023-winners-announced)

projects.title: My "Make with Ada"​ projects
projects.description:
My projects for "Make with Ada 2016" competition. I won the 2nd place prize and the
"Robert Dewar" special prize on the dependability criterion.

I also ported the GNAT Ravescar Small-foot-print Runtime library to NXP Kinetis microcontrollers:
https://github.com/jgrivera67/embedded-runtimes

patents.title: Optimized utilization of DMA buffers for incoming data packets in a network protocol
Dynamic runtime range checking of different types on a register using upper and lower bound value registers for the register
